title: The Flywheel (v3 recut)
logline: A case built exhibit by exhibit from public documents: why ChatGPT, which OpenAI says more than a billion people use every week, is nearly free, how your clicks, chats and code help train the next model, who gets steamrolled when the wheel turns, and the one asset no release can upgrade for you.
director_statement: v3 keeps the v2 concept, look, structure, narrator and cold open, and fixes two things the creator called out: (1) robotic voices: the archive reader and the 'for the record' reader are gone, no voice uses a filter preset or ElevenLabs effect, and no voices are stacked; quotes are shown on screen and the narrator reads the key phrase himself; (2) the energy dying in the middle: the cut is tighter, the narrator is performed forward-leaning, every exhibit gets its own score cue that steps up in tempo and weight, every chapter card and reveal lands on an impact, the music stays big under the voice (multiband ducking), and the only silence left is the 'Yours.' beat.

cast.purpose: The designed v2 narrator (kept: the creator loved it). Investigator building the case; in v3 he carries every claim AND every quote. Exhibits are performed [confident]: forward-leaning and propulsive, never shouting. Dry, no effects.
cast.design_prompt_v2: Male, mid-fifties, neutral General American accent. Warm, low baritone with a light natural grain and clear, precise consonants. A calm, plain-spoken documentary narrator, like an investigative journalist laying out evidence to one listener: quietly serious, measured, with natural pauses and a little warmth. Never theatrical, never a movie-trailer, announcer or detective-pastiche read, never gravelly for effect, never shouting. Can drop to a soft, clean whisper. Recorded close to a large-diaphragm microphone in an acoustically dead room: intimate and dry, with no reverb, no music and no background noise. An original voice that must not imitate any real actor, narrator or public figure.

cast.purpose: A user in the dark: a real, close whisper. No filter.
A tired young coder; returns in the closing to answer 'Train it.' in his own clear voice.
A busy user; also asks 'Summarize this.' in Exhibit B.
The user who whispered 'Help me say sorry.'; returns in the closing to answer 'Guard it.'
The user who asked 'Am I doing this right?'; returns in the closing to answer 'Move it.'
An illustrative, excited founder pitching a thin wrapper; cut off mid-sentence. Dry.

lines.caption: Scale built the engine. Bigger models. More data. More compute.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR

lines.caption: The free product was shaping the next one.

lines.caption: You use it.

lines.caption: The model improves. More people come. The wheel spins faster.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] Even your thumbs-up counts. In twenty twenty-five, a ChatGPT update added a reward signal from thumbs-up and thumbs-down data.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR

lines.caption: It helped make the model so flattering that OpenAI rolled the update back.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] You're not just the customer. You're part of the wheel.
lines.caption: You're not just the customer. You're part of the wheel.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] Startups rushed to wrap the models.
lines.caption: Startups rushed to wrap the models.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR

lines.caption: Then ChatGPT learned to read PDFs.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR

lines.caption: One reaction online: “Many startups just died today.”

lines.speaker: NARRATOR

lines.caption: A reaction, not a verdict. Thin wrappers were exposed. Strong companies got squeezed, or bought.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] Sam Altman's warning: bet that the models won't improve, and you'll get steamrolled.
lines.caption: Sam Altman's warning: bet that the models won't improve, and you'll get steamrolled.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR

lines.caption: Each model opens doors. The next release can close them.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] Then the wheel turned to the coders.
lines.caption: Then the wheel turned to the coders.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] The memos came. Use AI. Shopify: a baseline expectation. Microsoft, reportedly: no longer optional.
lines.caption: The memos came. Use AI. Shopify: a baseline expectation. Microsoft, reportedly: no longer optional.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] In twenty twenty-three, AI could fix about two percent of real GitHub issues on a benchmark.
lines.caption: In 2023, AI could fix about 2% of real GitHub issues on a benchmark.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] By February twenty twenty-six, Anthropic reported about eighty percent, for Claude Opus four point six.
lines.caption: By February 2026, Anthropic reported about 80%, for Claude Opus 4.6.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] Then Claude Opus five point five. Anthropic puts it at the level of its larger Fable model, on most work.
lines.caption: Then Claude Opus 5.5. Anthropic puts it at the level of its larger Fable model, on most work.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [curious] And your code, on personal plans?
lines.caption: And your code, on personal plans?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] GitHub believes the future of AI-assisted development depends on real-world interaction data. From developers like you.
lines.caption: GitHub believes the future of AI-assisted development depends on real-world interaction data. From developers like you.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [serious] So why is it nearly free?
lines.caption: So why is it nearly free?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] Investor billions. A race for users. Ads. Falling costs.
lines.caption: Investor billions. A race for users. Ads. Falling costs.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [serious] And part of the price is paid in data.
lines.caption: And part of the price is paid in data.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [whispers] Yours.
lines.caption: Yours.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] There's a switch. But most people never touch their defaults.
lines.caption: There's a switch. But most people never touch their defaults.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR

lines.caption: It's a trade. Often a good one. Just know what you're trading.

lines.text: [excited] So our app just calls the model—
lines.caption: So our app just calls the model—

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [confident] But if your plan is a thin wrapper on someone else's model... wait.
lines.caption: But if your plan is a thin wrapper on someone else's model... wait.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [serious] The wheel won't.
lines.caption: The wheel won't.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [warmly] Still. Go ahead. Build. Raise money. Ship.
lines.caption: Still. Go ahead. Build. Raise money. Ship.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: [warmly] But your biggest asset isn't on that list.
lines.caption: But your biggest asset isn't on that list.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Your attention. We now stay on one screen about forty-seven seconds before switching. Guard it.
lines.caption: Your attention. We now stay on one screen about 47 seconds before switching. Guard it.

lines.speaker: VOICES_5
lines.text: Guard it.
lines.caption: Guard it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Your mind. In Anthropic's own trial, coders learning with AI scored seventeen points lower on what they'd just learned. Train it.

lines.caption: Train it.

lines.text: Move it.
lines.caption: Move it.

music_cues.covers: COLD_OPEN + TITLE: the v2 cue, kept (the creator loved the opening)
EXHIBIT A: a steady ticking pulse that tightens to the reveal

positive_styles: steady low kick on every beat

music_cues.covers: EXHIBIT B: a mechanical loop that spins faster
EXHIBIT C: heavy and relentless, hard stop on the door
EXHIBIT D: the fastest cue, racing to a hard cut
EXHIBIT E ledger: a heartbeat pulse under the list, cut dead before 'Yours.'
EXHIBIT E fairness + VERDICT: from the sub drop after 'Yours.' to the peak on 'The wheel won't.'
CLOSING + END: an anthem, not a lullaby

transitions.description: Kept exactly: whispers, cut to silence, 'It looks like a gift', case file slam, braam, typewriter title.
A riser builds under the last line of each exhibit, a whoosh clears the frame, and the chapter card slams in on a trailer hit with a white flash and a camera punch. The next cue starts on the hit.
The door latch cuts to 0.25 s of black; the D card slams in with a keyboard storm.
A riser ends dead on 'like you.'; 0.5 s of black and silence; the E card slams in on a hit with a lone clock tick.
The ledger pulse cuts dead after 'paid in data'; 'Yours.' is whispered in silence; a sub drop restarts the score, which then builds without a break to the verdict.
'The wheel won't.' lands on the biggest hit of the film; reel runout; the film burns through to dawn.

sequences.title: Cold open: a billion whispers (0:00.0-0:21.1)
sequences.mood: Darkness and intimate unease: a sea of private requests, then dead silence, then one quiet voice and a question.
sequences.transition_in: Fade up from black on the projector motor starting (1.5 s pre-roll); the first bubble and the first whisper arrive together.

sequences.title: Main title: THE FLYWHEEL (0:21.1-0:27.1, music only)
sequences.mood: Weight and ceremony: the case file is opened, and it is made of public documents.
sequences.transition_in: The case file slams shut, then a hard cut to black; braam; the typewriter title with the sub-line 'A CASE IN FIVE EXHIBITS · ALL FROM PUBLIC SOURCES'.

sequences.title: Exhibit A: The Gift (0:27.1-1:10.0)
sequences.mood: Archival, slow-burn suspicion: sepia 16mm, with documents surfacing one by one.
sequences.transition_in: Projector-gate flicker into the archive-reel grade; chapter card 'EXHIBIT A · THE GIFT' (1.8 s).

sequences.title: Exhibit B: The Wheel (1:10.0-1:42.9)
sequences.mood: Mechanical and hypnotic: a loop closing, now with human voices in it; colder grade.
sequences.transition_in: Match-cut morph: the three timeline dots curve into the flywheel rim; a reel-change cue mark flashes twice; the grade shifts sepia to cold blue-grey.

sequences.title: Exhibit C: The Steamroller (1:42.9-2:11.9)
sequences.mood: Pressure, kept fair: reactions versus outcomes.
sequences.transition_in: The spinning wheel tears in a 0.4 s digital glitch into the chapter card.

sequences.title: Exhibit D: The Acceleration (2:11.9-2:51.9)
sequences.mood: Velocity: the tightest pulse, in a clean present-day look, ending in the company's own words to 'you'.
sequences.transition_in: Sound-motivated hard cut: a door's latch click cuts to black; the card appears as a keyboard storm rises out of nothing.

sequences.title: Exhibit E: The Price (2:51.9-3:17.8)
sequences.mood: A quiet ledger, then the price revealed in total silence ('Yours.'), then fairness: there is a switch, and it is a trade.
sequences.transition_in: Hard cut to 1.5 s of digital silence and black; a lone clock tick under the card 'EXHIBIT E · THE PRICE'.

sequences.title: The Verdict, a warning to builders: please, wait (3:17.8-3:33.2)
sequences.mood: Stillness and care: one illustrative founder is gently interrupted; the wheel keeps turning without us.
sequences.transition_in: No cut: a slow continuous push-in from the 'trade' statement onto an illustrative 'YOUR APP' card; HUD 'A WARNING TO BUILDERS'.

sequences.title: The One Asset (3:33.2-4:15.7)
sequences.mood: Light breaks in: warmth, the human scale, hope; the chorus answers itself.
sequences.transition_in: Reel runout and film burn-through into warm white; light leak; dark-to-dawn palette shift; shutters open onto birdsong.

sequences.title: End card (4:15.7-4:21.2)
sequences.mood: Resolution and quiet confidence; warm, with no stamp.
sequences.transition_in: Fade through warm white from 'Invest consciously.'; a pen is set down.
